title: Latency-budget vs Quality Playoff — MotionHealth Optimize Demo
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) with practical tradeoffs for MotionHealth's real-time triage API; discussed latency budgets, quality guardrails, rollout and fallback playbooks. Agreed to run 48-hour mixed-precision sandbox and share benchmark spreadsheet + security checklist.
topics: latency budget tuning and batching impact
security/compliance considerations: KMS, VPC, audit logs
action_items: Lena: share benchmark spreadsheet (int8/fp8 testcases + tokens) by 2027-11-05
Samir: provide sandbox access instructions and recommended load generator commands by 2027-11-04
Priya: share 5 representative prompt sets and acceptance criteria by 2027-11-06
Carlos: confirm VPC peering timeline and network access by 2027-11-08
next_steps: Start 48-hour Optimize sandbox run (MotionHealth team to provide prompts)
Redwood to send decision matrix and expected cost delta estimates
Schedule follow-up deep-dive after sandbox (week of 2027-11-15)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood Solutions Eng); Dr. Priya Raman (MotionHealth), Carlos Mendez (MotionHealth platform), Ava Liu (MotionHealth CTO), Jon Park (MotionHealth SRE)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Quick demo of Optimize console qprofiles. Focus on pairing latency budgets with quality thresholds. Customer is worried about triage endpoint latency under 120ms P95 and also needs <=2% quality regression from current baseline.

00:00 Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:04 Priya: Hi this is Priya, I'm head of ML at MotionHealth, hi Carlos, Ava, Jon here.
00:07 Carlos: hi all
00:09 Ava: hey
00:12 Samir: Samir here, I'll be doing the deep bits on the qprofiles and benchmarking.
00:15 Lena: Great. Today we'll run through Redwood Optimize, show how to create an INT8 and FP8 profile, run the console sampling and then talk about the rollout + fallback rules. We're mindful of your latency budget of, what did you say, 120 ms P95?
00:30 Priya: Yep that's right. and quality—we need to keep the triage accuracy close to current model, ideally within 1-2% top-line F1 drop.
00:38 Samir: Got it. Quick thing up front: when we say FP8 here we're talking about our mixed-precision FP8 path, it's usually better for generative fidelity but costs a bit more than int8. INT8 will give you the biggest unit cost savings but may show noise on sensitive prompts.
00:55 Jon: Just to be explicit, our infra is GCP us-west2 with private VPC peering, so network egress needs to be minimal; we'll likely want Dedicated or Private eventually.
01:05 Lena: Noted. We'll cover Dedicated latency profiles and Private deployment notes at the end. Alright Samir, show the console.
01:12 Samir: Opening Optimize console — ping if you don't see my screen. (few seconds of background clicking) Okay, top-left is the qprofile creation flow. You can start from a recommended template — we have one for real-time low-latency endpoints.
01:30 Samir: I'll create two profiles: MH-triage-int8 and MH-triage-fp8. first step is sample selection — I'm uploading a 200 prompt set (you can drag/drop).
01:45 Priya: we usually run on a 500 prompt set but 200 is fine for demo. real runs will be 2k to 5k.
01:52 Samir: makes sense. Console then runs a sampling job — it'll run each profile across the sample and collect metrics: per-prompt latency, token counts, and quality deltas against your baseline. this is where the console ties to your baseline evals.
02:07 Carlos: quick Q—how deterministic are these samples? if the transcript is slightly different do we get inconsistent deltas?
02:13 Samir: Good Q. sampling is pseudo-deterministic — same seed and same model artifact will be comparable. but note that when the runtime routes to an alternate kernel (eg. fallback to FP8 kernels), you can see small variance. Also the transcription engine (our internal metric calc) sometimes mismatches punctuation in evals, so we recommend using normalized tokenization and exact-match tolerant metrics for triage.
02:36 Priya: ok. show us the numbers.
02:38 Samir: Running the sampling job now... (progress bar) Alright first plot: latency distribution. INT8 median is 42 ms, P95 ~98 ms with small tail spikes. FP8 median is 58 ms, P95 ~125 ms. So FP8 is slightly over your 120 ms P95 target.
03:02 Ava: interesting. cost delta?
03:04 Samir: Roughly FP8 is ~1.4x cost of INT8 per-token ignoring batching; with our batching and KV cache it atypically narrows to ~1.2x. console shows an estimated monthly delta: INT8 projected $6.8k, FP8 $8.3k for your expected traffic.
03:20 Priya: And quality? what's the F1 delta?
03:22 Samir: For this sample, INT8 shows -2.5% F1 relative to baseline; FP8 shows -0.6% F1. Some prompts with numerical reasoning had larger deltas on INT8.
03:33 Priya: That's concerning — our SLA allows up to 2% drop, so INT8 could be risky without mitigations.
03:39 Samir: Exactly — that is where hybrid profiles and fallback rules help. You can create a primary INT8 profile with rules to route certain prompt classes to FP8 or to full-precision in edge cases. we recommend a policy: try INT8, if quality score below threshold then retry on FP8 or dynamic rollback.
03:58 Carlos: how do you classify prompt classes? KNN? regex?
04:02 Samir: Two ways: static classifiers from your tags (you can attach metadata to prompts) or dynamic runtime scoring. The console supports a small ML classifier — we call it the fidelity router — it uses features like prompt length, presence of certain keywords, or an embedding distance to canonical examples. You can also map by endpoint path.
04:20 Priya: ok show a failure case.
04:22 Samir: here's an example prompt where INT8 hallucinated a medication name; FP8 preserved it. You can see the token-level diff in the console, and the quality metric that triggered the rule.
04:33 Priya: hmm. that token-level diff view is helpful. can we tie that to our eval harness?
04:37 Samir: Yep, exportable CSV and direct API integration with your eval harness. We also keep per-profile snapshots to reproduce regressions.
04:45 (brief crosstalk)
04:50 Jon: network question — during a fallback do we pay double latency because of a retry? what is user-visible impact?
04:55 Samir: Good point. We support in-line fallback (single request that tries fast path and then transparent fallback without client retry), but that depends on runtime. The tradeoff is slightly higher P95 versus the user doing an explicit retry. Our in-line approach uses speculative execution on compatible hardware — that adds a small cost but reduces tail latency. For strict budgets we recommend canary + async recheck instead of immediate retry.
05:20 Ava: speculative execution sounds expensive. how does Redwood estimate cost impact?
05:24 Samir: Console shows expected cost/pathing matrix. For example speculative FP8 warm stand adds ~10% compute overhead but reduces user-visible error. The cost-line item shows both total tokens and compute-time equivalence.
05:35 Priya: let's talk about batching — our traffic is bursty, 60% small requests under 15 tokens, 40% long. How do profiles handle batching impact on latency?
05:47 Samir: Optimize wires in the serving runtime's batching profile. You can set max batch delay, prefer low-latency scheduling, or aggressive throughput. For short tokens you get great batching efficiency but it increases tail if you wait too long. In the console you can simulate traffic and see expected P50/P95 under different batching configs.
06:10 Carlos: do those simulations account for KV cache reuse? our workflow reuses context across calls frequently.
06:16 Samir: Yes — we let you configure KV cache hit rates; the sampler will adjust per-token latency based on cache hit scenario. For your workload if cache hit >60% the INT8 P95 improved to ~82 ms in our sim.
06:30 Priya: That's promising. show me how to set fallback rules end-to-end.
06:33 Samir: creating a policy — name: triage-fallback-v1. Condition: quality_score < 0.88 OR prompt_tag == "numerical". Action: route to FP8. Alternative action: if still below threshold, route to full-precision with async alert to team. We can set max retries and timeouts.
06:55 Priya: can we set SLO-based automatic rollback? for example if overall customer-facing error rate increases by X then auto-unset the INT8 profile.
07:03 Samir: Yes — rollout policies let you set health checks on quality metrics; if degraded beyond threshold for N minutes/weeks we automatically revert to previous profile and alert your SREs.
07:12 Ava: one more ask: our compliance team requires KMS integration and key rotation visibility. how does Redwood expose that for Private deployments?
07:20 Lena: I'll take that briefly. For Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSMs; audit logs are surfaced in the console and forwarded to your SIEM. We'll include SOC2 scope docs in the packet.
07:33 Priya: perfect. also, about the baseline — currently our baseline is a finetuned model on internal dataset. can Redwood ingest a private baseline for quality comparison?
07:42 Samir: Yes, you can upload your baseline artifact or point to a model id; the console will compare output against that baseline. For privacy we keep the comparisons ephemeral unless you opt to save snapshots.
07:53 (brief pause)
08:00 Samir: running a quick ad-hoc AB test in the console: I'm toggling a canary at 10% traffic to the INT8 profile with fallback to FP8 for flagged prompts. live metrics show a small uptick in tail latency but cost down.
08:18 Priya: what does the live metric chart look like?
08:20 Samir: (shares chart) P95 at 10% canary is 105 ms, cost delta ~-12% vs FP8 only. Quality delta is -0.9% F1.
08:30 Priya: ok that might be acceptable if we can pin the flagged prompt classes.
08:34 Carlos: On the security side, can we run the sandbox inside our VPC?
08:38 Lena: Yes, we can provision a Private sandbox in your VPC or do a short-lived peered sandbox for benchmarking. for the POC we often use private peering to make network conditions realistic.
08:49 Jon: any guidance for load generation? we want to mimic bursty mobile traffic.
08:53 Samir: We'll send a small load generator script (wrk + custom prompt feeder) that models your 60/40 short/long distribution and simulates jitter. It's part of the sandbox onboarding.
09:02 Priya: let's talk tolerance bands — if INT8 is -2.5% on 200 prompt sample but improves when cache hit rate is high, how do we quantify production risk?
09:13 Samir: Two suggestions: 1) long-running sandbox (48 hours) with traffic shaped to your production mix and KV cache settings, and 2) a weighted sample that focuses on high-risk prompt categories (medical references, numerical reasoning). Console will output per-category deltas so you can quantify risk per class.
09:33 Ava: would you help us set the acceptance criteria? we prefer something automated.
09:37 Samir: Absolutely. We can preconfigure an acceptance script that fails the profile if any critical category exceeds 1% regression or if P95 exceeds 120 ms for > 10 minutes.
09:48 Priya: that seems reasonable.
09:50 (ten minute jump in transcript to condensed discussion of internal notes and chat, transcription includes some errors)
19:50 Speaker 1: notes — Maya to draft rollout doc, check SSO SAML integration, include audit log retention options
20:02 Maya: yes I'll draft it, and include a sample canary policy
20:07 Carlos: quick vendor question — are you using Triton under the hood or a custom runtime?
20:11 Samir: our runtime is own-engine with kernel selection, we do integrate with Triton-compatible kernels sometimes; we optimize for continuous batching and kv cache management.
20:22 Priya: can we run a short performance deep-dive with your infra team? want to correlate our perf traces with Redwood traces.
20:29 Lena: yes, we'll schedule a performance sync.
20:33 Priya: also could you compute expected monthly cost delta for 6 months for both profiles?
20:36 Samir: will do — expect within 24 hours.
20:40 (more chatter about dates)
23:10 Samir: final notes — we'll provision the 48-hour sandbox, you'll provide the 2k prompt set and desired KV cache hit assumptions. We'll attach the benchmark sheet and an example policy.
23:22 Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
23:26 Lena: quick recap of action items and owners...
23:29 Lena: Lena to send benchmark spreadsheet and security docs; Samir send sandbox instructions and load generator script; Maya send rollout doc + SSO steps; MotionHealth to send prompt sets and confirm VPC peering window.
23:47 Priya: ok, we'll aim to have prompts by Friday.
23:50 Ava: thanks team, excited to see the sandbox results.
23:54 Lena: thank you all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the follow-up next week.
23:58 (meeting ends)
